question: Which of the following accurately represents India's trend in the Global Gender Gap Report 2025?

options.text: India slipped in its global rank
India joined the top twenty nations

solution:
The correct answer is __**India slipped in its global rank**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 
__ 

• The **Global Gender Gap Report** is published annually by the **World Economic Forum (WEF)**, which measures gender equality across four key dimensions: **economic participation and opportunity, educational attainment, health and survival, and political empowerment**. 

• India has seen a **slip in its global rank** in recent editions of the report, indicating a **widening gender gap** in areas such as workforce participation, political representation, and educational equality. 

• As per the latest trends, India’s performance has been particularly poor in **economic participation and opportunity**, where the gap between men and women has widened due to **low female workforce participation** and unequal pay. 

• In the **health and survival category**, India continues to struggle due to issues such as **sex ratio imbalances** and **access to healthcare for women**. 

• The decline in rank reflects broader systemic issues, including **social norms, cultural barriers**, and the impact of economic disruptions like the **COVID-19 pandemic**, which disproportionately affected women. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
__ 

• **Global Gender Gap Report:** 
 

• The report was first introduced by the **World Economic Forum (WEF)** in **2006** and aims to benchmark progress toward gender equality worldwide. 

• The index ranks countries based on their performance across **four dimensions**: economic participation, educational attainment, health and survival, and political empowerment. 

• In recent years, countries like **Iceland, Finland, and Norway** have consistently ranked at the top due to their progressive policies and cultural acceptance of gender equality. 
 
 

• **India's Position:** 
 

• In the **2023 edition** of the report, India ranked **127th out of 146 countries**, showing a decline from previous years. 

• India’s **economic participation and opportunity score** remains low, mainly due to limited access to leadership roles and unequal pay. 

• India’s **political empowerment score** is relatively better, attributed to the representation of women in the **Lok Sabha** and state assemblies. 
 
 

• **Impact of COVID-19:** 
 

• The **COVID-19 pandemic** exacerbated existing inequalities, pushing more women out of the workforce and increasing unpaid caregiving responsibilities. 

• Many women in India faced challenges such as **job losses, reduced income, and limited access to healthcare and education**. 
 
 

• **Government Initiatives:** 
 

• India has launched several schemes to bridge the gender gap, such as **Beti Bachao Beti Padhao**, **Mahila-E-Haat**, and **Stand-Up India**. 

• Programs focusing on **education, entrepreneurship, and healthcare** aim to empower women and reduce disparities. 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
 

• **Key Challenges:** 
 

• India’s low female labor force participation rate remains a major challenge in achieving gender equality. 

• Persistent issues such as **gender-based violence**, **discrimination**, and **patriarchal norms** hinder progress. 

• Lack of access to education and healthcare in rural areas disproportionately affects women and widens the gender gap. 
 
 

• **Recommendations:** 
 

• Promote policies that encourage **women’s economic participation**, such as flexible work arrangements and skill development programs. 

• Increase investments in **healthcare and education** for women, especially in rural and underserved areas. 

• Strengthen legal frameworks to address **gender-based violence** and workplace discrimination.
